worksheet.title: Extra or Missing Block
worksheet.subtitle: Ontario Math C3.2 — read, find, and fix code
worksheet.learning_goal: I can fix a loop that has an extra block or a missing block.

parts.title: Too many or too few blocks
text: Some bugs are not about numbers — they are about the BLOCKS inside the loop. There might be an EXTRA block, or a needed block might be MISSING.
Read what Bit should do, then check the inside blocks: is one extra, or is one missing?

parts.title: Bit should do clap, stomp — but this has an EXTRA block
parts.note: There is an EXTRA stomp. Bit does 6 stomps instead of 3. Remove the extra block.

parts.title: Find the extra block
parts.prompt: The loop should be clap, stomp — but it has clap, stomp, stomp. Which block is extra? How many stomps does Bit do now instead of 3? ______

parts.title: Find the missing block
parts.prompt: This should draw a SQUARE:  for i in range(4): bit.forward(50). But Bit draws a straight line! What block is MISSING inside the loop?

parts.title: Write the fix
parts.prompt: Add the missing block to fix the square. Write the line that goes after bit.forward(50):  bit.________(______)

parts.title: Challenge
parts.prompt: A square loop has an EXTRA turn:  for i in range(4): bit.forward(50); bit.right(90); bit.right(90). Bit just goes back and forth on a line. Why? What should you remove?

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Count the blocks inside the loop, not just the repeats. An extra block does too much; a missing block leaves the job unfinished.

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Students debug loops with an extra inside block (does too much) or a missing inside block (job unfinished) — in block and turtle contexts — and describe how adding/removing one block fixes the result (C3.2).

parts.title: Curriculum (Ontario Math 2020, Strand C3)
text: C3.1 — solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing code, including code that involves sequential, concurrent, and repeating events.
C3.2 — read and alter existing code, including code that involves sequential, concurrent, and repeating events, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: A block-coding app and/or Python Turtle projected; the printed worksheet + a pencil per student.

parts.title: Run it (about 30 min)
text: 1. Run the clap, stomp, stomp loop; count 6 stomps; remove the extra block.
2. Run the forward-only square — a line; add the missing right(90).
3. Students do Exercises 1–4 (Ex 4 is the stretch), solo or in pairs.
4. Share answers; land the big idea: check the inside blocks for extra/missing.

parts.title: Answer key (checked by the run-gate)
text: Ex 1 — the second stomp is extra; Bit does 6 stomps (remove one to get 3).
Ex 2 — the turn block (bit.right(90)) is missing.
Ex 4 (challenge) — two turns of 90 = a 180 flip each side, so Bit goes back and forth; remove the extra bit.right(90).

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: changing the repeat count when a block is extra/missing.
Support: list the inside blocks and compare one-to-one with the goal.
Extend: ask what a missing forward (only turns) would draw (Bit spins in place).

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The student spots an extra or missing inside block (not the count) and adds/removes one block to match the goal (Ex 1–3), explaining the extra-turn effect (Ex 4).
